components.name: OTP Input
components.description: One-time password input with a living SVG ripple border. Every keystroke nudges the outline, correct codes send a green wave across the boxes, wrong codes bounce red and shake. Validation, carets and all motion parameters are prop-driven.

variations.name: ripple
variations.description: Each box wears an SVG outline that behaves like a liquid surface — typing nudges it, moving to the next box hands the ripple off toward its right edge. Pass a validate function and the component choreographs the pending ring, the staggered success wave and the red shake by itself, then calls your onSuccess / onFailure.

props.name: length
props.description: Number of character boxes

props.name: mode
props.description: Which characters the boxes accept — alphanumeric uppercases as you type

props.name: masked
props.description: Render entered characters as dots

props.name: rippleOnType
props.description: Animate the border on every keystroke — off by default, so the ripple only plays for pending / success / failure

props.name: pendingRing
props.description: Oscillating ring while an async validate is pending — off by default, pending shows as border color only

props.name: caretColor
props.description: Caret color — drives the native bar caret and the fake block / underscore carets

props.name: caretShape
props.description: Caret style — bar is the native caret; block and underscore are rendered carets with a native-feeling blink

props.name: staggerMs
props.description: Delay between each box's green pulse in the success wave, in ms

props.name: maxAmplitude
props.description: Ripple height ceiling in px

props.name: bumpWidth
props.description: How localized the ripple bulge is, as a fraction of the box perimeter

props.name: decay
props.description: How fast ripples settle — higher is snappier

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius in px, shared by the box and its ripple outline

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Ripple outline stroke width in px

props.name: shakeDistance
props.description: Failure shake travel in px

props.name: validate
props.description: (code: string) => boolean | Promise<boolean> — called when all boxes are filled. Return or resolve true for success, false for failure; the component shows the pending border color while a promise is in flight, then plays the result animation

props.name: onSuccess
props.description: (code: string) => void — fired after the green success wave finishes. Put your post-verification action here (navigate, submit, close modal)

props.name: onFailure
props.description: (code: string) => void — fired after the red pulse and shake finish. By default the boxes have already been cleared and refocused (see autoClearOnFailure)

props.name: onComplete
props.description: (code: string) => void — fired once every time all boxes become filled, before validate runs

props.name: onChange
props.description: (value: string) => void — fired on every edit with the current joined value. Pair with value for controlled usage

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value — pair with onChange. Omit to let the component manage its own state

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value for uncontrolled usage

props.name: autoClearOnFailure
props.description: Clear the boxes and refocus the first one after the failure animation

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable all boxes. Inputs are also locked automatically while validate is pending

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Focus the first box on mount

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name announced for the group of boxes

variations.previewHint: Type or paste the code 123456 to see the success wave — anything else triggers the red double-pulse and shake. Use the DialKit panel to reshape the ripple, swap the caret to block or underscore, and recolor it.
features: Declarative validation: pass validate(code) returning boolean or Promise<boolean> — the component shows a pending ring while the promise is in flight, then runs the success or failure choreography and fires onSuccess / onFailure
Paste and SMS autofill aware: pasting a full code fills every box from the first, and autocomplete="one-time-code" lets mobile keyboards inject the code from a text message
Configurable caret: bar uses the native caret with your color; block and underscore render a fake blinking caret that restarts solid on every keystroke, exactly like a native one
Controlled or uncontrolled — pass value + onChange, or nothing at all and the component manages its own state
Failure shake ships as plain CSS that the shadcn CLI merges into your globals.css on install, with shake distance exposed as a prop via a CSS custom property
Accessible: role=group with per-box labels, aria-live announcements for checking / accepted / incorrect, and aria-invalid during failure
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — ripples become instant color states, the shake and caret blink are disabled
The ripple engine (RippleBorder) installs as a sibling file, ready to reuse for text inputs and search fields

components.name: Button
components.description: Animated buttons built on top of the shadcn/ui Button, each exploring a different animation pattern — a hover-triggered sparkle trail, a click-triggered confetti burst, and a hover-triggered scramble-text reveal.

variations.name: whimsical
variations.description: On hover or focus, five color-shifted sparkle particles launch along the button's border via CSS offset-path, each with its own speed, scale and landing spot.

props.name: mainHue
props.description: Hue (0-360) driving --main-color and every particle's derived color

props.name: decoSize
props.description: Base width of each sparkle particle, in px

props.name: timing
props.description: Base travel duration in seconds — each particle multiplies this by its own speed variation

variations.previewHint: Hover (or tab to focus) the button to see the five sparkle particles launch along the border.
features: Particles travel via CSS offset-path: border-box — they literally ride the button's own rounded outline, no hand-tuned path math
Each particle is an independent config (color, scale, end-offset, end-translate, speed) driving a data array — no per-particle conditional logic
Colors use CSS relative-color syntax (oklch(from var(--main-color) ...)) so a single mainHue prop repaints every particle consistently
Opacity follows a life-cycle keyframe (fade in, hold, fade out) so particles never pop in or out abruptly
Wraps shadcn/ui's Button (ghost variant) rather than replacing it — accepts every standard Button prop
Skips all particle motion under prefers-reduced-motion; the border color change remains instant

variations.name: confetti
variations.description: On click, a burst of color-varied confetti pieces launches from the button center — each with its own angle, distance and rotation — arcing up and falling back down under simulated gravity.

props.name: particleCount
props.description: Number of confetti pieces launched per click

props.name: baseHue
props.description: Base hue (0-360) the confetti palette's hue offsets are applied to

props.name: spread
props.description: Max travel distance in px before gravity pulls pieces back down

props.name: duration
props.description: Total burst duration in seconds

variations.previewHint: Click the button to fire a confetti burst. Click repeatedly — each click stacks its own independent burst.
features: Impulse-triggered on click, not continuous on hover — a one-shot celebratory animation rather than an ambient loop
Each particle gets an independent random angle, distance, rotation, size and shape (rect or circle), driving a data array — no per-particle conditional logic
y-axis uses a 3-keyframe rise-then-fall curve (easeOut up, easeIn down) to simulate gravity, while x and rotation animate in a single easeOut pass
Colors cycle through a fixed set of hue offsets from a single baseHue prop, giving a multi-color mix instead of monochrome confetti
Bursts are independent and stack — clicking again mid-animation launches a second burst without cancelling the first
Wraps shadcn/ui's Button rather than replacing it — accepts every standard Button prop, including variant
Skips the burst entirely under prefers-reduced-motion; the click still fires onClick

variations.name: scramble
variations.description: On hover or focus, the label's characters cycle rapidly through random glyphs before locking in to the real text one character at a time, left to right — a decode-style reveal built entirely from content substitution, no positional or color motion.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's label — scrambled on hover, then revealed character-by-character

props.name: frameDuration
props.description: Milliseconds between scramble frames

props.name: staggerFrames
props.description: Frames each subsequent character waits before locking in — controls how pronounced the left-to-right reveal looks

variations.previewHint: Hover (or tab to focus) the button to watch the label scramble and resolve left to right.
features: Purely typographic — no particles, movement or color change, just the label's characters substituting over time
Each character locks in at a later frame than the one before it (index * staggerFrames), producing the left-to-right decode reveal from a single interval loop
Spaces are preserved as-is and never scrambled, so multi-word labels stay legible mid-animation
Re-hovering mid-scramble restarts cleanly — the previous interval is cleared before a new one starts
Wraps shadcn/ui's Button rather than replacing it — accepts every standard Button prop, including variant
Skips scrambling entirely under prefers-reduced-motion; the label is shown as-is

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Animated accordion built on top of shadcn/ui. Replaces the CSS height transition with Framer Motion easing — fully accessible, keyboard navigable, drop-in ready.

variations.name: clip
variations.description: Two-layer card reveal — the question clips away via clip-path in the chosen direction, exposing the answer beneath. Click the answer to return.

props.name: direction
props.description: Direction the question clips away — horizontal (left) or vertical (up)

props.name: ease
props.description: Cubic-bezier easing curve for the clip animation

props.name: duration
props.description: Duration of the open animation in seconds (close runs at 60%)

variations.previewHint: Click a question to see it clip away and reveal the answer. Click the answer to return. Toggle between horizontal and vertical with the direction prop.
features: Two-layer card: question sits as an absolute overlay on top of the answer — no height measurement needed, answer's rendered height sets the card size
Exit is faster than enter — question clips away at 60% of the open duration so returning feels deliberate, not rushed
Direction is a single prop: horizontal wipes right-to-left, vertical wipes bottom-to-top — same constants object, no conditional logic in the animation
Pointer-events swap atomically: question layer is pointer-events:none when clipped, answer layer is pointer-events:none when covered
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all clip-path and translate animations disabled instantly
Fully accessible: AccordionPrimitive.Trigger handles aria-expanded and keyboard navigation

variations.name: drawer
variations.description: Each trigger lifts with a 3D spring when open, and the content slides up from behind it. Spring stiffness and damping are fully configurable via the DialKit panel.

props.name: stiffness
props.description: Spring stiffness — higher values snap faster

props.name: damping
props.description: Spring damping — lower values add bounce, higher values settle immediately

variations.previewHint: To adjust the spring feel, use the DialKit panel to change stiffness (snappier vs. looser) and damping (bouncy vs. settled).
features: Trigger lifts with a 3D perspective tilt when open — rotateX + y offset combine to create a physical card-lifting effect
Content slides from y: -24 with the same spring as the trigger, so both feel coupled and intentional
Exit is a fast ease-in snap — closing should feel decisive, not linger
Chevron rotates 180° on open with a separate duration transition — icon state change is simpler than a spring
whileHover lifts the card slightly even when closed — affordance that this is interactive
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all springs and transforms disabled instantly
Fully accessible: keyboard navigation and ARIA attributes come from Radix unchanged

variations.name: ease
variations.description: Content panel opens and closes with a cubic-bezier easing curve. Use the DialKit easing editor to draw any curve — ease-out, ease-in-out, or a custom bezier.

props.name: ease
props.description: Cubic-bezier easing curve for the height animation

props.name: duration
props.description: Animation duration in seconds

variations.previewHint: To change the easing curve, open the DialKit easing editor and drag the handles to shape the cubic-bezier curve.
features: Exit is faster than enter — closing should always feel decisive, users want content gone, not lingering
Open plays as two beats: height snaps first, content fades in after a fixed gap — prevents text appearing while space is still forming
Icon morphs with ease-in-out, content opens with ease-out — different curves for different roles: one is transforming in place, the other is entering the screen
Opacity uses linear easing — at short durations easing curves on opacity are imperceptible, linear is honest
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — all animations are disabled instantly when the user has reduced motion enabled in their OS
Fully accessible: keyboard navigation and ARIA attributes come from Radix unchanged
